report.source_text: A decision was taken to switch enoxaparin to unfractionated heparin (UFH) intravenous infusion 6000 units/6 hourly because of the risk of bleeding, in view of the micro-haemorrhagic infarcts noted on imaging, keeping the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) ratio between 2 and 3. Enalapril was increased to 5 mg two times per day, and carvedilol 3.125 mg two times per day was also added as heart failure treatment. Antiplatelets were stopped considering that the patient was on UFH intravenous pump. The patient improved from a neurological point of view by the following day. He became more coherent and able to follow commands.

clinician.final_diagnosis: severe COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by multiorgan thrombosis including myocardial ischaemia, left ventricular thrombus, intracranial thrombosis and mesenteric involvement despite prophylactic anticoagulation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old man with dyslipidemia and diabetes mellitus presented to the emergency department 7 days after a positive SARS-CoV-2 swab with acute central compressive chest pain (pleuritic in nature), dyspnea at rest, lethargy, myalgias, and non-productive dry cough. On admission, vital signs showed sinus tachycardia (113 bpm), mild hypoxemia (92% on room air), and physical examination revealed fine end-inspiratory crepitations at both lung bases consistent with pneumonia. Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 13.06, CRP 115, procalcitonin 0.192), hyperglycemia (25 mmol/L), and critically, grossly elevated D-dimer (5483 ng/mL) and highly elevated troponin (504 ng/L) indicating both hypercoagulability and myocardial injury. Chest X-ray confirmed diffuse patchy airspace shadowing consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia. ECG showed right heart strain with new-onset right bundle branch block. Initial echocardiogram revealed a globular dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 35% and akinetic apical, anteroseptal, and anterior walls, consistent with myocardial ischemia. The initial clinical impression was acute coronary syndrome (ACS) complicated by myocarditis on a background of COVID-19 pneumonia. By ICU day 3, repeat transthoracic echocardiogram documented a large apical mural thrombus (left ventricular thrombus) with apical akinesia. On the same day, MRI of the brain revealed established infarcts involving the left temporal lobe and right occipital lobe with minor foci of micro-haemorrhagic transformation in the left temporal lobe, documenting intracranial thrombosis. By ICU day 4, imaging findings of micro-haemorrhagic infarcts prompted a change in anticoagulation strategy from enoxaparin to unfractionated heparin (UFH) intravenous infusion at 6000 units every 6 hours with APTT ratio maintained between 2 and 3. The patient showed neurological improvement by ICU day 5, becoming more coherent and able to follow commands. The final diagnosis encompasses severe COVID-19 pneumonia with multiorgan thrombotic complications (myocardial ischemia with left ventricular thrombus, intracranial thrombosis with micro-haemorrhagic infarcts, and mesenteric involvement) that occurred despite prophylactic anticoagulation.
